```sh
# ~/.config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh
# Source: dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# `tsum` — AI-powered overview of every tmux session. Thin POSIX wrapper
# around ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py (the core script does the
# capture, LLM call, 10-min caching, and rendering).
#
# Why a wrapper at all (not just an alias):
#   - `-i` / `--interactive` adds an fzf picker on top of the script's
#     `picker` mode and calls `tmux switch-client -t <sess>` on Enter.
#     fzf piping is awkward to express as an alias.
#   - The wrapper does an early-return-silent dance when tmux isn't on PATH
#     (cron, fresh boxes pre-ansible) so calling code can be unconditional.
#
# See:
#   - dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py (the core)
#   - docs/shells/aliases.md (`tsum` row)
#   - dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh (shares AICAP_* env vars)
#   - dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (this file's slot-61 neighbour)

# Skip silently if tmux isn't installed — POSIX-shared file, may be sourced
# inside cron / Docker / headless SSH long before ansible bootstrapped tmux.
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

tsum() {
    _tsum_script="$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py"
    if [ ! -x "$_tsum_script" ]; then
        printf 'tsum: %s missing or not executable. Run `chezmoi apply` first.\n' "$_tsum_script" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    _tsum_interactive=0
    _tsum_forward=""

    # POSIX-portable arg parse — `getopts` can't do long flags, so do it by
    # hand. Everything except `-i`/`--interactive` is forwarded as-is to the
    # Python script (which has its own argparse).
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            -i|--interactive)
                _tsum_interactive=1
                ;;
            -h|--help)
                cat >&2 <<'EOF'
tsum — AI-summarize every tmux session

USAGE
    tsum [list]                 print one-block-per-session summary (default)
    tsum picker                 print TSV (session<TAB>line) for fzf piping
    tsum -i | --interactive     fzf picker; Enter switches client to that session
    tsum -d | --deep            include last 20 lines of active pane in LLM prompt
    tsum -r | --refresh         bypass the 10-min cache
    tsum --dry-run              print what would be sent to the LLM (no API call)
    tsum --no-cache             don't read or write the cache

ENV
    AICAP_AGENT, AICAP_*_MODEL  pin / override the agent (shared with aifix/aiblock)
    TSUM_CACHE_TTL              seconds, default 600
    TSUM_TIMEOUT                seconds, default 60

CACHE
    $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/<hostname>.json
EOF
                return 0
                ;;
            *)
                # Quote each forwarded arg with single quotes; embedded single
                # quotes get the '\'' dance so eval-time re-parsing is exact.
                _tsum_forward="$_tsum_forward '$(printf %s "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")'"
                ;;
        esac
        shift
    done

    if [ "$_tsum_interactive" -eq 0 ]; then
        # Plain mode — let the script render to stdout/stderr directly.
        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" $_tsum_forward"
        return $?
    fi

    # Interactive: picker | fzf, switch on Enter.
    if ! command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'tsum: -i needs fzf on PATH; falling back to plain output.\n' >&2
        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" $_tsum_forward"
        return $?
    fi

    # Force `picker` mode regardless of what got forwarded (silently strip
    # `list`/`picker` from the forwarded args by re-running with picker as
    # the explicit first arg).
    _tsum_selected=$(
        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" picker $_tsum_forward" \
            | fzf --ansi \
                  --delimiter='	' \
                  --with-nth=2 \
                  --preview='printf "%s\n" {2}' \
                  --preview-window='down:3:wrap' \
                  --prompt='session> ' \
                  --header='Enter: switch  /  Esc: cancel' \
                  --no-multi
    )

    [ -z "$_tsum_selected" ] && return 0

    # First TAB-delimited field is the session name.
    _tsum_target="${_tsum_selected%%	*}"

    if [ -z "${TMUX:-}" ]; then
        # Outside tmux: attach to the chosen session instead of switch-client.
        tmux attach-session -t "$_tsum_target"
    else
        tmux switch-client -t "$_tsum_target"
    fi
}
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tmux popup helper for the "AI session summary" entry in menu-session.sh.
#
# Why a separate script (not inlined in the menu): CLAUDE.md hard rule —
# tmux's display-menu parser treats `{}`, `;`, and `|` as delimiters, and
# the fzf --bind expression below uses all of them. Keeping the pipeline
# in its own file eliminates the parser-quoting trap entirely.
#
# Companion files:
#   - dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py  (the core)
#   - dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh                 (the `tsum` shell wrapper; same pipeline for -i)
#   - dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh          (the calling menu)
set -euo pipefail

script="$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py"

if [ ! -x "$script" ]; then
    printf 'AI session summary: %s missing or not executable. Run `chezmoi apply`.\n' "$script" >&2
    sleep 2  # popup auto-closes too fast otherwise
    exit 1
fi
if ! command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'AI session summary: fzf required for picker mode. (apt/brew install fzf)\n' >&2
    sleep 2
    exit 1
fi

# `|| exit 0` — Esc / Ctrl-C in fzf exits 130; we want the popup to just
# close quietly, not surface a non-zero exit.
selected=$(
    "$script" picker "$@" \
        | fzf --ansi \
              --delimiter=$'\t' \
              --with-nth=2 \
              --preview='printf "%s\n" {2}' \
              --preview-window='down:3:wrap' \
              --prompt='session> ' \
              --header='Enter: switch  /  Esc: cancel' \
              --no-multi
) || exit 0

[ -z "$selected" ] && exit 0

# First TAB-delimited field is the session name.
tmux switch-client -t "${selected%%	*}"

```

```text
648	## Tmux Integration
649	
650	> Requires tmux + OSC 133 markers in the pane's scrollback (emitted by [`02_shell_integration.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — if missing, run `exec zsh` to reload). All three functions print to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`) AND copy to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge. Shell-level counterparts of the `prefix + M-y` / `M-i` tmux bindings — see [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 133](../tools/tmux/README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style).
651	
652	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
653	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
654	| `cpout [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's output** (default N=1). Accepts positional integer for lookback |
655	| `cpcmd [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's input line** (default N=1). Reads zsh history so works outside tmux too |
656	| `cpblock [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's full block** (prompt + input + output). Default N=1 |

660	## AI Capture
661	
662	> One-shot pipeline: capture a past block (via `cpblock N`) and pass it to a coding-agent CLI (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent) in non-interactive / advisory mode. Agent auto-detected in the order listed; override with `-a AGENT`. Prompt override via `-p PROMPT`. Agent reply goes to stdout (pipe-friendly: `aifix | tee /tmp/advice.md`), status line to stderr.
663
```

Done. Here's what was added:

**Files (chezmoi-managed, all deploy via `chezmoi apply`):**
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` — core (PEP 723 / `uv run --script`, `rich>=13.9`). Subcommands `list` / `picker`, flags `-d/--deep`, `-r/--refresh`, `--dry-run`, `--no-cache`. Reuses the same `AICAP_*` env vars as `aifix`/`aiblock` (claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent fallback). 10-min cache in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/<host>.json` keyed by SHA-256 over the (session × window-cmd) tuple — cache invalidates when structure changes, ignores idle navigation. JSON-mode LLM call with metadata-only fallback on parse failure / no agent / timeout.
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary-popup.sh` — small bash script for the tmux popup (kept separate per CLAUDE.md "complex commands must live in their own script": fzf binds with `{1}`/`|` would trip the `display-menu` parser).
- `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh` — POSIX `tsum` wrapper (both shells get it). Same flags as the Python; `-i/--interactive` does picker→fzf→`switch-client` (or `attach-session` if invoked from outside tmux).

**Modified:**
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh` — converted from inline `exec tmux display-menu` to `rows=(…)` array (matches `executable_menu-agents.sh` pattern); appends "AI session summary" (key `u`) at the bottom-with-separator, gated on the popup script being executable so it hides on hosts that haven't applied yet.
- `docs/shells/aliases.md` — row added under **Tmux Integration**.

**Verified locally:**
- Python AST parse ✓, `bash -n` ✓, `sh -n` / `bash -n` / `zsh -n` on the wrapper ✓.
- `uv run --script … --dry-run` ran end-to-end on this host — pulled 4 real sessions, prompt construction is correct.
- `chezmoi diff` clean: only the three new files + the menu-session.sh edit (the unrelated `.codex/config.toml` mode/marketplaces drift is pre-existing).

```sh
exec zsh                   # so the new 61_tmux_summary.sh is sourced
tsum --dry-run             # audit what's sent — no API call
tsum                       # first real run (LLM hit, cache write)
tsum                       # cache hit, <500ms
tsum -i                    # fzf picker, Enter switches
# tmux: prefix + Space → Sessions → "AI session summary"
#   ↑ also retest at ~22-row terminal height per the menu-too-tall rule
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-12 06:58:07Z)**_

Two thoughts before changing the default:

**Bug visible in your `--deep` dry-run**: the `chezmoi [6 windows]` session's "recent output" is showing **its own previous `tsum --dry-run` output** — because window 6 is the pane running `tsum`, so `capture-pane` grabs whatever just scrolled by, including the script's own output. With deep-default this would happen on every invocation from the current pane, which means the LLM sees its own prompt format in the input and the summaries for the "current" session become unreliable. Worth fixing regardless (skip capture when the target pane equals `$TMUX_PANE`).

**Recommendation: keep --deep opt-in.** Two reasons that haven't changed:
1. **Secrets leak risk** — your output already shows lazygit panes with commit messages and remote URLs; on another box that could be `aws sts` tokens, `.env` cats, sudo prompts, anything in the active pane's scrollback. Metadata-only sends only paths + commands.
2. **Marginal quality lift** — looking at your actual `tsum --deep` output, three of four summaries (`Dotfiles`, `Chinese chess`, `agent-skills`) were inferable from metadata alone (path + commands like `opencode`, `lazygit`, `nvim`). Only `vibe/2026-04-29-ssh-bbs` benefited from deep (noticing the cwd mismatch), and metadata already shows that mismatch in the cwd column.

The middle ground would be a `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` env var (or `AICAP_TSUM_DEEP=1` for namespace consistency) you can set in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` so it's deep-by-default on your boxes without me flipping the global default. Want me to:
1. Fix the self-capture bug, and
2. Add the env-var opt-in?

**To use deep-by-default**, add this to `~/.shellrc.adhoc`:
```sh
export TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1
```
Then `tsum` is deep, `tsum --shallow` reverts per-call. `chezmoi apply` to pick up the script edits — your shell function will re-source on next `tsum -h` since it's defined fresh each shell load.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-12 07:04:05Z)**_

Good idea. Here's the proposed design — let me know if anything needs adjusting before I wire it in:

**Three-tier `closability` field in the LLM response** (added to each session object alongside `summary`):

| Tier | Glyph | Meaning | Triggers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `safe`  | 🟢 | Nothing important — close freely | Only idle shells / `zsh`,`bash`,`fish` alone; lazygit; `tail -f`,`htop`,`watch` monitors; detached >7 days |
| `check` | 🟡 | Review before closing | Editor open with a filename; attached but currently idle; recent commits to a worktree; deep-mode shows `[+]` modified marker |
| `keep`  | 🔴 | Active work — do not close | Coding-agent CLI as cmd (`opencode`/`claude`/`codex`/`aider`); long-running process (`python`,`node`,`npm run dev`,`docker compose up`,`pytest`,`cargo run`); attached with recent build/test/dev-server output |

**JSON schema extension** (cache version bumps to `v2`, old entries invalidated gracefully):
```json
{ "session": "…", "summary": "…", "closability": "safe|check|keep",
  "closability_reason": "≤50 chars why",  "important_windows": [...] }
```

**Rendering changes:**
- **list mode**: prepend the glyph, color the session name green/yellow/red, append the reason in dim. The "keep" tier gets a soft underline so it pops at-a-glance even if you're glyph-blind.
  ```
  🟢 chezmoi             *  [ 6w] Dotfiles edits — adding tsum feature
        └ w2: git — lazygit                                 (idle shells only)
  🔴 vibe/chinese-chess     [ 3w] Active opencode session, mid-task
        └ w1: agents — opencode running                     (agent conversation in progress)
  ```
- **picker mode**: glyph embedded in the TSV preview column so you scan tiers in fzf.
- **fallback** (LLM failed): uses ⚪ + no color, so the layout is consistent.

**Heuristic that's just-conservative-enough**: when in doubt, prompt instructs the LLM to pick `check` rather than `safe`. We don't want a false "safe" rating that nukes someone's work.

**Out of scope for v1** (ask if you want either):
- `--sort=closability` flag (groups keep→check→safe so active work shows first)
- `--only safe` filter (list candidates to bulk-close)
- A "kill all safe sessions" tmux menu action — destructive, deserves its own confirmation flow

Sound good as proposed, or do you want different tier names / glyphs / a default sort by tier?

Everything wired up. Summary of what shipped in this round:

**Schema (cache bumps to `v2`, old caches degrade gracefully):**
```json
{ "session": "…", "summary": "…",
  "closability": "safe|check|keep",
  "closability_reason": "≤50 chars why",
  "important_windows": [...] }
```

**Prompt heuristics** sent to the LLM:
- `safe` — only idle shells / lazygit / monitoring / detached >7 days
- `check` — editor open, attached idle, unclear state (conservative middle)
- `keep` — coding-agent CLI running, long-running process, attached + editing
- Explicit "when in doubt, pick check" rule so false-safe is rare

**Rendering:**
- list: 🟢/🟡/🔴 glyph + green/yellow/red colored session name; `keep` rows underlined for glyph-blind terminals; reason appended in dim italic.
- picker: glyph in the fzf preview column.
- fallback (LLM unavailable): ⚪ neutral glyph, `--sort=closability`/`--only` emit a stderr warning instead of silently dropping.

**New flags:**
- `--sort {alpha,closability}` — alpha is default (tmux's natural order); closability orders keep→check→safe with stable alphabetical within tiers.
- `--only {safe,check,keep}` — single-tier filter. Pairs nicely with picker mode: `tsum picker --only safe -i` lets you fzf-pick a safe-to-close session.

**Updated:**
- Python script: `closability` field, prompt preamble, cache `_CACHE_VERSION = "v2"`, three new ANSI/rich tier maps, `_apply_view()` helper, `_render_fallback()` helper, argparse extensions.
- `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh`: `--help` block + EXAMPLES section showing the killer combos.
- `docs/shells/aliases.md`: row updated with the new flags.

**To use:**
```sh
chezmoi apply
exec zsh                            # re-source the wrapper
tsum -r                             # force fresh LLM call (cache bumped to v2)
tsum --sort closability             # active work first, safe-to-close at bottom
tsum --only safe                    # "what can I nuke right now?"
tsum picker --only safe -i          # fzf among safe sessions, Enter switches
```

**One UX wrinkle I noticed in your output** — when you switched from `tsum -r --deep` to `tsum --sort closability` (no `--deep`), the second invocation tried a fresh LLM call (you Ctrl-C'd it). That's because the cache file is single-slot per host, and the `deep`-flavoured signature overwrote the `shallow` one. So toggling `--deep`/`--shallow` always invalidates the cache.

Two ways to fix if it bugs you:
1. **Two cache slots** — `<host>-shallow.json` and `<host>-deep.json`; flipping between modes hits cache for both. Tiny change (5 lines).
2. **Embed deep flag in signature** but keep one file with multiple entries indexed by sig — more flexible but more code.

Not urgent — say the word if you want #1, otherwise it stays as-is.
